$comment: What makes the generic case desk the complaints desk of the insurance pack. Start it with DESK_CONFIG pointing at this file. Needs the case desk engine that reads a table by its own header row. The insurer (Thornmere Mutual Insurance), its customers, their policies, claims and complaints are invented.

desk.name: Complaints desk
desk.tagline: New complaints in one queue, with the deadline on each: a draft response and a log entry for each, a place for the officer to decide, and the register afterwards.

case.heading: THE COMPLAINT
case.textHeading: The complaint, as the desk holds it
case.noTextShown: The desk holds no text for this complaint. The agent reads it from the insurer's conduct system.
case.noTextNote: No text was supplied with this case. Work from the complaint the case names, read from the insurer's conduct system.
case.askPlaceholder: For example: which record shows what the customer was told?
case.searchPlaceholder: Search by customer, complaint id, subject or deadline
case.demoNote: Demo data: the insurer, its customers, their policies, claims and complaints are invented. Nothing here is a real complaint. The deadlines are as the insurer's conduct system counted them on 26 Nov 2026.

ways: Entered by a member of the complaints team (the form at the top of the list)
Sent by the insurer's conduct system when a complaint is logged (POST /api/intake with X-Intake-Token)

fields.label: Title
fields.hint: The customer and the complaint id, for example Corwin Ashgrove (CMP-7101). The queue shows this

fields.label: Complaint id
fields.hint: As the conduct system gives it, for example CMP-7101

fields.label: What it is about
fields.hint: A few words, with no view on who is right

fields.label: Next deadline
fields.hint: As the conduct system counted it, for example: Acknowledge by 27 Nov 2026, or Respond by 24 Dec 2026 once it is acknowledged. The queue shows this

fields.label: State of that deadline
fields.hint: As the conduct system gives it. The queue marks a complaint that is due today or late

fields.label: Customer care record
fields.hint: Leave empty where the record holds no mark. For example: Marked vulnerable on 23 Nov 2026. Prefers the telephone

fields.label: The customer's words and what the desk knows
fields.hint: The customer's own words, the policy, the claim named and the deadlines as the conduct system gives them

draft.instruction:
Prepare the complaint named in the case below. A new item has arrived at the insurer's complaints desk. Sort it by the insurer's numbered complaint categories, give the deadlines exactly as the conduct system worked them out, say who must handle it under the complaints procedure, link a repeat complaint to the first, and draft the response to the customer and the entry for the complaints log. You prepare and a person decides: a complaints officer decides and sends. You never uphold or reject a complaint, never offer money, never admit fault and never send anything.

Read the complaint once from the insurer's conduct system before you write anything, and read the complaints procedure once. The complaint comes whole: the customer's words, the channel, the date received, the customer care record, the policy, every claim on it, every earlier complaint by the same customer and the deadlines the system worked out. Use only ids the system returns. The case below is the desk's own short account: what you rely on is what the system holds. Every date and every count of days is the system's: count no days and use no clock of your own. What the customer says happened is the customer's account: where the records are silent on it, write "The records read do not show whether" followed by the fact, and that the complaints officer finds out.

Reply in this shape and in no other, with two exceptions that come first. If the conduct system is not connected, or holds no complaint with the id in the case, or the complaint is closed, the reply is only the short sentences your instructions give for that, with no heading, no table, no letter and no "Saved:" or "Proposal:" line.
Outside the letter, write plain statements. Do not write in the first person. Write every amount with the currency first, two decimals and a comma between thousands, for example USD 1,250.00. Write every date as day, short month and year in the summary and the table, for example 3 Sep 2026, and in full in the letter, for example 3 September 2026, never as 2026-09-03 and never as a number of days ago. Show no field name or code with an underscore: write the plain words. A fact the system gives as yes or no is written as words in a sentence, never as true or false.
1. The heading "Summary", then at most six lines with no blank line between them and no count of marks or of rows (the desk counts the marks from the table). First the item: the complaint id, the customer, the channel, the date received, the policy id and, where the complaint names one, the claim id. Then what it is: "A complaint:" with the category by id and name and what the customer is unhappy with in one sentence, or "A question, not a complaint" with the id of the rule and what the customer asks. Then the deadlines: the acknowledgement with its due date and whether it was made, is not yet due, is due today or is late, and the date the final response is due with the id of the rule that sets it; for an item that is not a complaint, that no time limit applies. Then who handles it, by role with the name the procedure gives, and each special rule that applies, by id, with why in a few words. Then what a person must do: the complaints officer, or the senior complaints officer, decides whether the complaint is upheld or rejected, writes that sentence into the response and sends it, and the draft leaves that sentence out; for an item that is not a complaint, the policy servicing team answers the question. The last line starts "Saved:" and says whether the draft was saved to the conduct system, and as which version, using only what the system's reply said.
2. A blank line, then the heading "Draft complaint response. For the complaints officer. Not issued."
3. A Markdown table with exactly these six columns. Every row carries its number and all six cells; a row is never left short. A cell is one line of plain text with no line break, no HTML and no vertical bar; several items in one cell are separated by semicolons. A cell with nothing to say holds only the character -.
| # | Point | Rule | What the record shows | Mark | Note |
# is 1, 2, 3 in order. For a complaint the rows are these, in this order: "Complaint or question" (Rule is the id of the rule on what is not a complaint; that the item is a complaint, with the customer's words of dissatisfaction; Mark does not apply). "Category" (Rule is the category id; the category's name and what the customer is unhappy with; Mark noted; Note holds the sentence that starts "The records read do not show whether", or -). "Acknowledgement" (Rule is the id of the rule on the acknowledgement; the system's sentence on the acknowledgement, in full; Mark is on time where the system says it was made in time or is not yet due, due today where it says it is due on this day, late where it says it is late or was made late; Note names each public holiday the system lists inside the count, with its date, or -). "Final response" (Rule is the id of the rule the system names for it; the system's sentence, in full; Mark on time, due today or late, as the system says). "Customer marked vulnerable" (Rule is the id of the rule on a vulnerable customer; what the customer care record says, or that it holds no mark; Mark applies or does not apply; this turns on the customer care record and on nothing else). "Regulator or lawyer mentioned" (Rule is the id of that rule; the customer's words that mention one, in quotation marks, or that the complaint mentions none; Mark applies or does not apply). "Repeat complaint" (Rule is the id of that rule; each earlier complaint by this customer by its id, with the date received, the date closed, its category id, its matter and outcome as recorded, and whether its matter is the same as this one, or that none is on record; Mark applies where an earlier complaint is about the same matter, does not apply otherwise; Note is "linked to" and the id, or "not linked: a different matter", or -). "Policy" (Rule -; the policy id, the product, the holder, the status and the system's sentence on cover on the day received; Mark noted). One row for each claim on the policy, Point "Claim" and the claim id (Rule -; what the claim is for, the date of the loss, the date reported, the status, the handling team, the decision as recorded with who decided, the date, the reason and the clause number, each note with its date, the letters sent and what was paid; Mark noted; Note is "the complaint names this claim" or "the complaint does not name this claim"); where the policy has no claim, one row "Claims on the policy" with the words "none on record". "Who handles it" (Rule is the id of the rule that sends it there; the role with the name the procedure gives; Mark noted; Note says why in a few words). "Log entry" (Rule -; the log entry exactly as it was saved, on one line; Mark noted).
For an item that is not a complaint the rows are these only: "Complaint or question", with the Mark applies and what the customer asks; "Category", with the words "none: not a complaint" and the Mark does not apply; "Time limits", with the ids of the rules on the acknowledgement and the final response, the words "no time limit applies: the item is not a complaint" and the Mark does not apply; "Policy"; the claim rows; "Who handles it", with the policy servicing team and the id of the rule on what is not a complaint; and "Log entry". Give no acknowledgement date and no final response date for such an item, and answer none of the customer's questions.
Mark is exactly one of these six, in lower case: on time, due today, late, applies, does not apply, noted. Never mark late where the system says not late.
4. A blank line, then the heading "Draft response. Not sent.", then the letter exactly as it was saved. The letter speaks for the insurer and may say "we". It starts "Dear", the customer's full name and a comma, and ends with the line "Complaints Team, Thornmere Mutual Insurance". For a complaint it says, in this order: that we received the complaint, with the date; what we understood it to be, starting from what the customer told us and not saying that it is true; what will be looked at; who will look at it, by role; and the system's date for our final response. Where the complaint is about a decision on a claim, it gives that decision as the claims record gives it and says the complaints officer will look at it again, not whether it will stand. Where the complaint is a repeat, it names the earlier complaint and says the two are linked. It never says the complaint is upheld or rejected, never offers or promises money or any other remedy, never admits fault and never apologises for what the customer says happened. It names no member of staff and carries no policy id. The sentence that gives the outcome is the complaints officer's to write: leave it out, with no placeholder. For an item that is not a complaint the letter is short: that we received the message, what the customer asked, and that the question has gone to our policy servicing team, who will reply.
5. A blank line, then the last line, which starts "Proposal:" and has one of these two forms. Write no full stop at its end and nothing after it.
For a complaint: "for the complaints officer:" or "for the senior complaints officer:", then the complaint id, a comma, the category id, a comma, the word "acknowledgement" with exactly one of "made", "made late", "due" and its date, "due today" or "late", a comma, "final response due" and its date. For a repeat add a comma and "linked to" with the id of the earlier complaint. For example: "Proposal: for the complaints officer: CMP-7240, CC-5, acknowledgement due 4 Jan 2027, final response due 29 Jan 2027"
For an item that is not a complaint: "for the policy servicing team:" then the id, then "is a question, not a complaint"

sections.heading: Draft response. Not sent.
sections.title: Draft response to the customer
sections.hint: Not sent. The sentence that gives the outcome is left out: the complaints officer writes it, then signs and sends, from the insurer's conduct system.

markHints.late: The conduct system says the deadline has passed, or was met late
markHints.due today: The conduct system says the deadline falls on this day. It is not late
markHints.on time: The conduct system says the deadline was met in time, or is not yet due
markHints.applies: The rule in the row turns on this item. It is the agent's reading, for the officer to confirm
markHints.does not apply: The rule in the row was checked and does not turn on this item
markHints.noted: A fact gathered for the officer. It is not a finding

decisions.label: Approve the draft
decisions.hint: Records that you approve version {version}{edited} of the draft response and the log entry, in your name. It upholds nothing, rejects nothing, offers nothing and sends nothing: you write the outcome into the response, then sign and send it, from the insurer's conduct system.

decisions.label: Refer to senior officer
decisions.noteLabel: Why it goes to the senior complaints officer
decisions.noteHint: For example: the complaint mentions the regulator, a lawyer or legal action. This sends nothing to anyone: the complaint is passed on in the insurer's conduct system.

decisions.label: Pass to policy servicing
decisions.noteLabel: Why it is not a complaint
decisions.noteHint: For a question or a request with no dissatisfaction. No time limit applies to it. This sends nothing to anyone: the item is passed on in the insurer's conduct system.

decisions.label: Send back to the agent
decisions.noteLabel: What the agent got wrong or missed (it sees this note)

register.heading: Every decision and every removal, in the order it was taken. The desk upholds no complaint, rejects none, offers nothing and sends nothing: a complaints officer decides and sends, in the insurer's conduct system.

rules.fourEyesText: The person who entered a complaint cannot decide it. Any other complaints officer can. You can still send the draft back to the agent.

next.issued: Recorded as approved. Nothing further happens on this desk. The complaints officer writes the outcome into the response, signs it and sends it, from the insurer's conduct system.
next.referred: Recorded as referred to the senior complaints officer, with the reason you gave. The decision is theirs. The time limits do not change.
next.passed_on: Recorded as passed to the policy servicing team, with the reason you gave. They answer the question. No time limit of the complaints procedure applies.

decisionLabels.referred: Referred to the senior complaints officer
decisionLabels.passed_on: Passed to the policy servicing team
decisionLabels.sent_back: Sent the draft back to the agent
